title: Christopher Nolan Is Finally Coming to India. The Odyssey Premiere Brings Him, Matt Damon and Tom Holland to Mumbai.
excerpt: After twenty years of Indian fans filling IMAX halls for him, Nolan makes his first-ever India premiere appearance — and Mumbai joins London, Paris and New York on the global tour.
body:
For two decades, Indian fans have done everything short of building Christopher Nolan a shrine. They filled IMAX halls for Interstellar, turned Oppenheimer into a cultural event, debated Inception's spinning top in college canteens, and queued at 3,200 rupees a recliner for The Odyssey tickets that went on sale before the film even had a trailer in heavy rotation. And in all that time, the man himself never once set foot in the country for a premiere.

!Matt Damon — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

That changes this July. Christopher Nolan is coming to Mumbai.

"Expect paparazzi scrums, a flurry of "Tom Holland eating vada pav" content, and at least one viral clip of Damon attempting a Hindi phrase."

The news, confirmed on June 17, is that Nolan will attend the India premiere of The Odyssey at PVR Icon IMAX, Phoenix Palladium — his first-ever premiere appearance in India. And he isn't coming alone. Matt Damon, who leads the film as Odysseus, Tom Holland, who plays his son Telemachus, and Oscar-winning producer Emma Thomas — Nolan's wife and lifelong creative partner — are all on the guest list. For a country that treats Nolan as something close to a deity of the multiplex, this is the visit fans had stopped daring to hope for.

!Tom Holland — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

Mumbai joins London, Paris and New York as an official stop on The Odyssey's global premiere tour.

Read that sentence again, because it's the part that matters. Universal Pictures and the filmmakers have placed Mumbai alongside the traditional triumvirate of premiere cities. India is no longer an afterthought market that gets a dubbed release a week late. It's a headline stop on a global rollout — a recognition of how much of The Odyssey's pre-release momentum has been generated by Indian audiences in the first place.

!Christopher Nolan — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

And that momentum has been staggering. Advance bookings, which opened in IMAX on June 8, have already doubled Oppenheimer's records. Ticket prices have soared to as high as 3,200 rupees for recliner seats in Mumbai, while a Tamil Nadu government cap holds Chennai prices to a relatively gentle 508 rupees — where shows are vanishing the instant they go live. In the United States, AMC reported its biggest first-day ticket sales for any studio release since 2022, achieved more than a month before the film opens. The Odyssey is shaping up to be the kind of theatrical event the post-pandemic box office keeps being told no longer exists.

The film's hook is irresistible to a certain kind of cinephile: it is the first feature in history shot entirely on IMAX cameras, a technical milestone Nolan reportedly spent nearly twenty years working toward. He's taking Homer's foundational epic — the decade-long voyage of Odysseus, King of Ithaca, struggling home after the fall of Troy — and rendering it at a scale the format has never attempted. The cast is a Nolan-verse fever dream: Damon as Odysseus, Holland as Telemachus, Anne Hathaway as Penelope, with Zendaya as Athena, Robert Pattinson as Antinous, Charlize Theron as Circe, plus Lupita Nyong'o, Jon Bernthal and Samantha Morton filling out the ranks.

The choice of Damon and Holland as the travelling ambassadors is shrewd. Damon is Hollywood royalty with a CV — Good Will Hunting, the Bourne films, The Martian, Ford v Ferrari, Oppenheimer — that spans exactly the prestige-meets-popcorn register Indian audiences adore. Holland, meanwhile, is Gen Z catnip; the Spider-Man star arriving in Mumbai will set Instagram on fire regardless of which epic he's promoting. Expect paparazzi scrums, a flurry of "Tom Holland eating vada pav" content, and at least one viral clip of Damon attempting a Hindi phrase.

For the diaspora, the release logistics are simple and generous: The Odyssey opens in cinemas worldwide — India included, in all formats — on July 17, 2026. NRIs in the US, UK and Canada will watch it the same weekend as audiences in Mumbai, many of them in the same IMAX format that has driven the global frenzy. If you've been meaning to make the pilgrimage to a true IMAX screen rather than the "liemax" digital approximations, this is the film that justifies the drive.

There's something quietly fitting about The Odyssey — a story about the long, arduous journey home — being the film that finally brings Nolan to India. After twenty years of Indian fans showing up for him, the director is, at last, showing up for them. King Odysseus took ten years to reach Ithaca. Nolan took about that long to reach Mumbai. Both, it seems, were worth the wait.
